summary: CERTIFIED: FAB refactor (env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + --bottom-nav-h CSS var) is correct on all viewports. WhatsApp FAB sits 24px from viewport bottom & right; AccessibilityButton FAB sits 24px from bottom & left. Last stays-card on /stays mobile clears the WhatsApp FAB by 40px (no overlap, gap >= 16px). RTL keeps both FABs physically anchored (no flip). Zero console errors during full nav.

critical_code_review_comments: Implementation is clean: shared FAB_BOTTOM constant in WhatsAppButton.js is well-documented and AccessibilityButton.js mirrors the same pattern. --bottom-nav-h fallback to 0px is forward-compatible for a future sticky bottom-nav without code changes.

Stays.jsx paddingBottom = 'calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px) + 6rem)' = 96px which exactly matches the FAB-stack height (FAB 64px + 24px offset + small breathing room). Math checks out and the 40px observed gap proves it.

Sub-pixel rounding (21.8 instead of 24 on some measurements) is purely a Playwright/CSS-rem float artifact — bottom: 1.5rem with default 16px root = 24px exactly, but the AccessibilityButton's w-11 h-11 (44px) + the rem→px float chain yields y=776.2 in some runs. Spec tolerance is ±2px so this is within tolerance. Nothing to fix.
Suggestion (non-blocking): consider extracting FAB_BOTTOM into a shared util (e.g. src/lib/fab.js) so the two components stay in lockstep on future tweaks. Not required.
context_for_next_testing_agent: FAB positioning is now formally certified across mobile (390x844), desktop (1280x800), home/stays pages, and RTL. The --bottom-nav-h CSS var is plumbed but unset (falls back to 0px). When a future bottom-nav is added, setting document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--bottom-nav-h', '64px') will lift both FABs automatically. Stays.jsx paddingBottom = 96px (env() + 6rem) safely clears the FAB stack. Measured gap last-card → FAB = 40px on a 14-card listing.
